National Assembly
Upper House
Twenty-ninth Session
Complete Minutes of Proceedings
Magh 28, 2082
Wednesday
Meeting Number - 1
The meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:18 hours under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
(13:18 hrs)
The proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly will now begin. Honourable members, the Zero Hour has been scheduled. I have allocated one minute each for every Honourable member to speak during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress):-
(13:19 hrs)
Respected Chairperson Sir, the general public is expressing concern and anxiety about whether a fair, peaceful, and fear-free environment will be maintained for the upcoming House of Representatives election scheduled for Falgun 21, 2082. As the election approaches, incidents are increasing daily. News has emerged that on Magh 26, 2082, a pistol, two rounds of bullets, approximately one lakh rupees in cash, and banned items were found inside the Siraha prison. Similarly, on Magh 27, 2082, an attack occurred on a team of armed police who had gone to Birgunj, Parsa, to recover illegally smuggled goods. Three police personnel were injured due to the attack and vandalism of police vehicles by a group of traders. This attack is a serious challenge to the rule of law. An attack on security personnel is not a normal incident. If the very bodies responsible for enforcing the law become insecure, how safe will ordinary citizens be? Through you, Mr. Chairperson, I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to this serious matter. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Ghanashyam Rizal.
(13:20 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Ghanashyam Rizal (Nepal Communist Party, Unified Socialist):-
(13:20 hrs)
Respected Chairperson Sir, I am deeply saddened by the news of the tragic death of 12 passengers, including Man Bahadur Tamang from my home district of Dolakha, Bhimeshwor Municipality Ward No. 8, and others from Ramechhap and Okhaldhunga districts, in a bus accident where a passenger bus fell into the Tamakoshi River in Manthali Municipality Ward No. 6, Ramechhap district, on Magh 27, 2082. I offer my heartfelt condolences to all those who lost their lives in this tragic incident and express deep sympathy to the bereaved families. I wish the injured a speedy recovery. I also wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal, through you, Mr. Chairperson, to expedite and make effective the treatment and relief efforts. Respected Chairperson Sir, as the election approaches, black marketers have started causing hardship to the public by creating artificial shortages of daily necessities and increasing prices. Through you, Mr. Chairperson, I wish to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal to monitor the market and take action against the culprits. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
(13:21 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson Sir,
(13:21 hrs)
I commend the Government of Nepal and the Election Commission for their preparations to complete the election on Falgun 21. However, analyzing some recent decisions and actions of the Government of Nepal, a situation has arisen where there is doubt about whether this election will be fair and free from manipulation. The government has made a controversial decision to release on bail a candidate who was in jail according to a court verdict for allegedly defrauding voters of millions of rupees. The Non-Resident Nepali Association (NRNA) conference, which usually happens ten years in advance, is being organized by the government just before the election. These and similar decisions raise the question of whether the government is inadvertently showing partiality towards a particular party and candidate in the election. Therefore, through you, Mr. Chairperson, I wish to advise the Honourable Prime Minister: Prime Minister, please realize your national responsibility and do not deviate from the right path. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Rukmini Koirala.
(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Rukmini Koirala (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Respected Chairperson Sir,
(13:22 hrs)
Information has been received that on Saturday night at 12 AM, an elephant entered from the jungle in Shivasatasi Municipality Ward No. 19, Jhapa, Koshi Province, causing terror by entering people's homes, eating and destroying crops like paddy and maize, and causing destruction by killing people. Megharaj Rai, aged 45, from that ward, died due to the elephant attack. His wife, mother, and 3 children are safe. I offer my heartfelt condolences to the deceased and express deep sympathy to the family. We are constantly facing human casualties due to human-wildlife conflict. I urge the government to provide compensation and manage elephants or wildlife, considering these losses. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Renu Chand.
(13:23 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Renu Chand (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):- Respected Chairperson Sir,
(13:23 hrs)
According to the police in Chauchowk, 13 people died in a bus accident carrying wedding guests near Puchundi Municipality Ward No. 7, Baitadi. In Ramechhap, 12 people died and 8 were injured in a bus accident near the Tamakoshi River in Manthali Municipality. I offer condolences to the deceased and wish the injured a speedy recovery. I also draw the attention of the government to arrange appropriate amounts for relief to the families of the deceased and for the treatment of the injured. My question to the government is: accidents happen when the weather is bad, accidents happen when the weather is good, accidents happen due to overloading, accidents happen due to negligence, accidents happen due to traffic rule violations. Even when we summon ministries and ministers to parliamentary committees, helplessness is displayed there. What is this predicament? I wish to draw the government's serious attention to this matter. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress):- Respected Chairperson Sir,
(13:24 hrs)
I wish to express my heartfelt gratitude to the Right Honourable President Ram Chandra Paudel for protecting the constitution and bringing the country onto a constitutional path when the protector of Nepal's constitution, the Right Honourable President, was in a comatose state. I wish to draw the attention of the government, through this esteemed house, to create an environment where voters can cast their votes peacefully and fearlessly in the upcoming House of Representatives election on Falgun 21. I also extend my best wishes for a happy political and personal life to the Honourable members who are about to bid farewell after successfully completing their tenure, thereby enhancing the glory of this esteemed house. We will continue the commendable work you have initiated. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari (Nepal Communist Party, Maoist Centre):-
(13:26 hrs)
Respected Chairperson Sir, on Tuesday, a passenger bus traveling from Manthali, Ramechhap Ward No. 6, towards Okhaldhunga, fell into the Tamakoshi River from a narrow road at Mathanetar, Bhaluajor, around 10:30 AM, resulting in the death of 7 men and 4 women, totaling 12 people, and injuring 8 others. The deceased include the couple Bhim Bahadur Tamang and Janumaya Tamang, their relatives, and the bus owner Dipendra Basnet from Ramechhap, Lipu, Tamakoshi Rural Municipality Ward No. 7, as well as residents of Dolakha, Sindhuli, and Okhaldhunga. I express deep condolences for this tragic incident and wish the injured a speedy recovery. I demand that the government provide relief assistance to the families of the deceased and pay serious attention to the increasing road accidents across the country. Thank you. Greetings.
Right Honourable Chairperson:-
(13:27 hrs)
The turn of Honourable members to speak during the Zero Hour has now concluded. I would like to inform Honourable members that there will be no Special Time in today's meeting of the National Assembly. Honourable members, in accordance with the constitutional provision, one-third of the Honourable members will be retiring on Falgun 20, 2082, after completing their six-year term. The process of Honourable members who still wish to speak about their experiences gained through parliamentary practice in the House and committees, and other contemporary issues, will continue. I will provide time for the remaining Honourable members who wish to present their experiences. For this, I have allocated 12 minutes to each Honourable member. First, Honourable Member Devendra Dahal.
Honourable Mr. Devendra Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Respected Chairperson Sir,
(13:28 hrs)
I am pleased to stand at this rostrum of the National Assembly today and share some of my thoughts. Our term, along with 19 other members, began on Falgun 21, 2076. Due to the biennial elections of this National Assembly, new members have also been elected. I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to them through this rostrum. As our Honourable Chairperson mentioned, our term is ending on Falgun 20. During this period, I wish to present some matters from three perspectives within the allotted time: first, my experiences and the fields that have impacted me; second, in the context of some good traditions that have been initiated; and third, some suggestions. Firstly, I have expressed my views and opinions on various contemporary issues presented in this House at different times, and I have also participated in discussions on bills presented in the House. Parliamentary responsibility was my primary responsibility in this National Assembly. As a member of this House, I also had the opportunity to serve as the Minister for Physical Infrastructure and Transport for 14 months. I have explored the challenges of being in parliament and working in government. Through this, I have gained at least some understanding of the problems in Nepal's infrastructure sector, which will enable me to work with some expertise in addressing the challenges and solutions for Nepal's infrastructure in the future. While working, I had the opportunity to deeply study the gap between the country's situation, the nation's circumstances, and the aspirations of the people, as well as the expectations of the state and the mindset of the bureaucracy. Therefore, in essence, this House has been a university for me. I believe that the matters I have raised in this House will contribute to the strengthening of democracy, the enactment of necessary people-centric laws, the resolution of pressing public issues, and the agendas of national consolidation, development, construction, and prosperity. The evaluation of how much these have contributed will surely be done. I myself will also review this. Respected Chairperson Sir, I now wish to discuss another aspect of this House. I believe that this House will continue its positive aspects.

The continuity will be maintained, and I believe it will continue. When the parties present here raise issues in this assembly, whether personal or party-related, their concerns are heard. Your honor has played an important role in this. I thank you for that. I urge that this continuity be maintained. The proposal for a resolution on matters of public importance has brought parties together on certain common issues, and these have been passed by consensus. I believe this will also continue. Honorable Chairperson, I would now like to share a few things about this assembly. The National Assembly, which is a model of inclusivity, representing Dalits, women, backward regions, persons with disabilities, and ensuring balanced regional representation, is truly a proud federal parliament. Does its role match its position in parliamentary affairs? A serious review of this is necessary. While the Constitution of Nepal provides for it, it is also seen as an assembly of experts. Is it truly an assembly of experts? In practice, it does not appear so. It must truly be made an assembly of experts, and this is in the hands of the members of this assembly. Firstly, parties or the concerned voters must elect experts, and if that does not happen, we must try to become experts ourselves. We are 19 members who are about to bid farewell, so what is our role? Our role is to provide suggestions. To suggest that it would be good to proceed in a certain way. To make the role of this assembly effective, it is also necessary to correct the flaws in Articles 111, 105, and 110 of the Constitution. There is a discriminatory provision when a bill is presented in one assembly and sent to another after being passed. It is also necessary to end that. The time for discussing a bill and sending it back should be the same for both houses. However, for a bill originating from the House of Representatives, a time limit of 60 days is set for the National Assembly. There is no time limit for the House of Representatives. I have repeatedly raised this issue: we passed a bill as a private bill and sent it to the House of Representatives. However, that bill has not yet been discussed, nor has there been any hearing on it. In a way, the House of Representatives has, to use a less appropriate word, digested that bill. That bill has been digested and could not even be presented. This has weakened the dignity of this assembly. Attention must be paid to this, and since this is a constitutional provision, we must amend the constitution and move forward. And to make this assembly effective, I would like to suggest that the members of this assembly should not waste time by engaging only in political speeches. As political representatives, that may be necessary at times, but should we reconsider spending all our time on it? My suggestion is that we should focus on issues essential for the state, present them with deep study and evidence-based data, and work to bring them forward analytically. What should be the education and health policies of Nepal? What is Nepal's position in terms of development? What is the development model going forward? What is our country's agricultural policy? What should be the industrial policy? What policies should be adopted for production growth, transportation, import substitution, and export promotion in our country? While drafting the Constitution of Nepal, we envisioned a socialist-oriented state system in Article 4. What policies should be formulated to bring Nepali society to that state? I think it would be good to discuss such issues. Did we pay attention to this issue when we discussed it yesterday? It could also be a part of the review while we are here. Political parties have not been able to provide a model of socialism. The NCP (UML) has put forward the concept of 'Happy Nepali' for the establishment of socialism. But that is not enough for prosperity. A detailed explanation is necessary. According to our constitution, what model of socialism can be implemented in our country? The members of this assembly can also provide that model. After the promulgation of the new constitution and the implementation of federalism, the problems seen in the implementation of federalism at all three levels have not been studied and presented. Although federalism is a good system, dissatisfaction with federalism is gradually increasing. Is federalism or the three-tiered government a burden on the people? This debate has begun. It cannot be said that this dissatisfaction will not reach the level of abolishing federalism. Can the number of ministries in the federal government be reduced to strengthen federalism or reduce the public dissatisfaction? Or what needs to be done? I believe the views of the members of this assembly should also be heard. What can be done to develop industries, create employment, increase production, and develop a self-reliant economy to ensure food, shelter, and clothing? The views of the members of the assembly should be heard. Why is a policy not being made to invest the billions of rupees in remittances earned by Nepalis in production and employment? I believe the members of this assembly should share their views on what kind of policy should be made. Exports are far exceeding imports, yet foreign exchange reserves are increasing. What is the reason for this? Analytical views should be presented. I believe this assembly is the most authoritative forum for generating ideas, discussions, seminars, gatherings, or interactions that provide direction for nation-building. Therefore, we must understand these issues and convey a message that all the ideas presented here have come from the representatives of the people. And finally, this may be my last opportunity to express my views as a Member of Parliament in this assembly. I heartily thank the Honorable Chairperson and this assembly, its secretariat, for giving us this opportunity. And until today, or for as long as our term lasts, I have felt that we have completed the term of this assembly with mutual cooperation, understanding, and without much disagreement or debate. We have also shown records of this assembly functioning even when the House of Representatives was closed due to its own closure. Therefore, all honorable members should take this seriously and share these matters with the incoming honorable members to further elevate the dignity of this assembly, to establish this assembly as an assembly of experts. If we can provide such ideas, saying that the National Assembly is an assembly of experts that can provide national ideas, it would be even better. And here, apart from us 19, the term of other honorable members has not ended, and the remaining 19 will come here. I hope that the National Assembly will perform its duties in a way that sends such a message. And finally, I would like to conclude my remarks by extending my heartfelt thanks to the Honorable Chairperson. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ganga Kumari Belbase. (13:40 hrs) Honorable Mr. Ganga Kumari Belbase (Communist Party of Nepal, Maoist Centre): (13:41 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, time is observed in the National Assembly. The assembly and committees are held on time, and all organized programs are held on time, as everyone knows. Representatives of the government, stakeholders, have all praised the National Assembly for its punctuality. Sometimes, our assembly members arrive before the program organizers. The Zero Hour has been well observed. Approximately 40 percent of the members speak on contemporary issues. Zero Hour has been utilized for very important matters. In the Special Time, the time allocated to all members is pooled and spoken. On average, all members speak in turn. Since parties coordinate the time through consultation, this management is good. Emergency time has been well utilized. Since prior information is given to the Chairperson and the Secretariat, it has helped in organizing the assembly. The utilization of emergency time has also helped to prevent international and national events that occur between assemblies, as well as protests and obstruction of the house. When the House of Representatives was obstructed, the practice of clarifying the issue of protest, how it is done, and why it is done in the emergency time of our assembly, and not obstructing the assembly, was also achieved through the proper use of emergency time. The rules of the National Assembly have provisions for Provincial Time on the first and third Fridays of the month. This is a time for members to speak on the issues, possibilities, good practices, and various matters of the province from which they were elected. Provincial Time is arranged for discussing inter-provincial relations and the relationship between the electoral college and the constituency. Provincial Time has proven to be a milestone in strengthening federalism. Honorable Chairperson, it is felt that the National Assembly is an important assembly and committee for cooperation, coexistence, and coordination. All four committees in the National Assembly have started holding joint meetings and discussions after reviewing the agenda. Cooperation is ongoing between the committees of the House of Representatives and the National Assembly based on subject matter. A joint meeting was held between the Social Development Committee of Karnali Province and the Legislation Committee regarding post-legislative scrutiny. The Legislation Management Committee presented on post-legislative scrutiny, and information about the main work done by the provincial committees, learning, curiosity, and good practices were discussed. Coordination and cooperation are ongoing between the federal, provincial, and local levels. This is mainly being done by the National Assembly and its committees. The National Assembly is an unbroken succession. It is constitutionally an unbroken succession. The term of office of us 19 members, including the formation process and election process, is ending on the coming February 21st. 18 have already been elected. As soon as the farewell is over, the new members will assume office. Since there are members with terms of 2 years, 4 years, and 6 years, the experience of work, continuity of work, development of knowledge and skills, and the search for new work and knowledge continue uninterruptedly. Significant work has been done in the 8 years of the National Assembly and my 6-year tenure. It is clear that there will be no duplication of work as there is an unbroken succession in all work. I hope the committees will remain engaged in search, monitoring, and research. The four committees are engaged in their work according to their annual work plans. How many laws remain to be made according to the constitution? What subject matter is being drafted by which ministry? After the country moved to federalism, how many laws does each ministry need to make? Have the directives given to the government been implemented? What percentage has been implemented, what is likely to be implemented, and what is impossible to implement? The committees are evaluating their own work. The work done by the committees is reviewed. Learning by doing,

The opportunity to learn is also being provided. A special committee, federalism implementation, monitoring and evaluation, by forming a parliamentary special committee, programs were conducted with all seven provinces and representative local levels, and a research-based report was prepared and discussed in the assembly. The Rt. Honorable Prime Minister addressed and made the assembly effective. Regarding national pride projects, studies, reports, and the suggestions given by them, to efficiently perform the federal parliamentary responsibilities, attention has been drawn to the ministry for the establishment of a parliamentary desk and information has been received about the establishment of a contact desk in the ministry. A program against cancer and the Kathmandu Declaration were issued. Information was provided about the need for research to reduce human-wildlife conflict and to amend the National Parks and Wildlife Conservation Act, 2029. Study and evaluation report on the implementation status of Sustainable Development Goals in Nepal, study and report on National Integrity Policy, report on strategies to be adopted for Nepal's graduation from Least Developed Country to Developing Country status in 2082, report on the status and management of vehicles under the control of the Traffic Office, a draft bill has been proposed as legal arrangements are necessary regarding the rights of the Dalit community. Public policy, appropriate legislation, government assurance study subcommittee is being formed and work is underway, and reports are in the preparation stage. Research and study of national importance documents, archive management, and historical and archaeological heritage are being conducted. I want to inform you about the various statuses of legislative bills originating in the National Assembly. Bills originating in the National Assembly, bills that have been authenticated, bills withdrawn by the government, bills enacted when the House of Representatives is not in session, legislative bills are in various statuses, and in terms of the law-making process, discussions are held with the proposing ministry and drafters while making laws. Discussions are held clause by clause with stakeholders, experts, committee members, and amendment members, followed by report writing, reading, discussion, and passing. Amendments are made to subjects including the preamble of the Act. The time of commencement of the Act is specified. Provisions for the measurement of laws are made. To reduce inappropriate legislation, if it is necessary to write or make it, it is arranged in the Act itself. Emphasis is placed on the principle of inclusivity. The committee is conducting work on the measurement and research of Act implementation. It is necessary to conduct training on Act measurement in provinces and local levels, and provinces and local levels have also advanced the work of Act measurement. Regarding the background of making the Act, the things we have paid attention to in the measurement of Act implementation are: what is the background of making the Act, and what is the impact and effect of the law in evaluating the law? What are the improvements and modifications to be made in the Act? The work done by the committee will remain as documentation, the committee will move forward continuously by making a work plan, and it will be added to the priority sequence. It moves forward in terms of the previous term, the current term, and the terms of future members. Work is done without party divisions, simply and easily. The National Assembly operates according to the schedule, the committee works by preparing a checklist, and if the government is to fulfill the commitments made in the House and committees and implement the suggestions, then I believe that progress will be made in all three tiers of government, all seven provinces, and all local levels. I entered from the 5th session of the House and have been continuously present and working hard until the 19th session. I have been cooperating with the Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson, and Committee Chairpersons. I thought I would get an opportunity to work as a chairperson once in my 6-year term. The arrangement for the election of the chairperson every 2 years is fine. Legislative bills remain in the National Assembly, but there is a situation where they are enacted when the House of Representatives is dissolved. It is not good for legislative bills prepared by spending a lot of resources to become ineffective in the final stage. Many meticulously prepared bills like the Civil Service Bill and the School Education Bill have become ineffective. It would be good if arrangements could be made for important bills to move forward from that stage. I have also worked hard to form a Women's Coordination Committee in the National Assembly. It would be good if it could be formed with consensus and consultation. Rt. Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Vice-Chairperson, the management of the House is being done well. I want to thank you for this. I express my gratitude for the patience, restraint, knowledge, skill, and intellect of all the Honorable Members. I thank the Secretary General of the Federal Parliament, the Secretary of the National Assembly, the Secretary of the Secretariat, the Secretaries of the Committees, the Undersecretaries, Officers, and all the staff of all the branches and sub-branches, and I express my gratitude to all the security personnel and media persons. I express my gratitude to the Rt. Honorable Prime Minister, Ministers of the Government of Nepal, government agencies, non-governmental organizations, various cooperative groups, individuals, personalities who participated as experts in committees and provided support, and all stakeholders. The success is the result of everyone's joint investment. Thank you. (13:42 hrs) Presiding Officer: Honorable Vice-Chairperson Ms. Bimla Ghimire. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Tulsa Kumari Dahal. (13:52 hrs) Honorable Mr. Tulsa Kumari Dahal (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honorable Chairperson Sir, as I present my 6 years of experience in this esteemed House, I want to thank and remember my party, the CPN UML, the then party leadership, the members of the Madhesh Press, the chiefs and deputy chiefs, chairpersons and vice-chairpersons of the local municipalities. I pay respect to the martyrs who sacrificed for the Federal Democratic Republic, and it is our duty to protect this system. I believe it is also our responsibility to work in accordance with the spirit and intention of the constitution made through the Constituent Assembly. I want to thank the Rt. Honorable Chairperson, the Honorable Vice-Chairperson, the Secretary General of the Federal Parliament, the current Government of Nepal, and concerned parties for their efforts to convene the 19th session of the National Assembly, which was suddenly postponed due to the specific circumstances of the country. We have had the opportunity to share our experiences as members of the National Assembly who are completing their 6-year term and are about to retire. I thought, 'We don't even get this much.' The 6-year period is a long time. Personally, this time feels long to me. During this period, I have gained positive experiences from the cooperation with national politics, the overall situation of the country, the ruling parties and their leadership, the condition of political parties, parliamentary committees, honorable members of the House, and the secretariat members. Along with positive experiences, I am also happy. This is my first experience in public service. If I have hurt anyone, made a mistake for any reason during this period, I request forgiveness. While being in this House and committees, I have gained some positive experiences and some negative feelings. In terms of positive experiences, I feel that we have been able to conduct in-depth studies within the defined scope of 2 out of the 4 committees of the National Assembly. The Committee on Delegated Legislation and Government Assurance, whose name was changed to the Committee on Public and Delegated Legislation by the second amendment to the rules, has this experience of working in this committee. I also served as a member and chairperson of the Legislation Management Committee. Committee meetings are held on time, and House meetings, with few exceptions, start and end on time. In accordance with the provisions of the committee's rules, the law-making process monitors and inspects the government's actions, provides suggestions, and gives directives on necessary matters. This House is known and understood as a house of wise, learned, and mature individuals. The House is mostly conducted in a peaceful environment, and the House has been conducted with the use of dignified language, mutual coordination, and cooperation. I wish for this legislative process to continue. During this period, the COVID pandemic, a new type of epidemic, and the loss of life and property in the country have saddened me and made me feel unwell. Some commitments and resolutions made to the public could not be fulfilled. This is because the constitution itself has curtailed some rights of this House, and there was no equality among the honorable members. There was also a problem in the government's perspective. The Federal Parliament has two Houses, and there was a problem in the understanding and implementation that they have equal responsibility and importance. Honorable Chairperson Sir, analyzing myself, I feel that I have gained a lot of knowledge and skills from this House. I feel that I have fulfilled my responsibilities to the best of my ability, consciousness, and capacity. I could not manage international experience, nor did I get the opportunity, and this is an undeniable truth. I would like to thank the Honorable Vice-Chairperson for remembering that I was able to visit China, a neighboring country, once. I have gained positive experiences within the country. Although I represent the women's sector from Madhesh Province, I have always raised my voice against discrimination and inequality towards women and will continue to do so. I believe that efforts have been made to the best of my ability in policy and law-making for the rights and solutions to the problems of various classes, strata, sectors, and communities. However, the standard of living of the people has not changed significantly. Although some arrangements have been made in terms of policy in areas like roads, water, electricity, health, and infrastructure, the people in all places are still not able to live a comfortable life. Honorable Chairperson Sir, the National Assembly has been facilitating the law-making process through experience sharing, interaction, and discussion through committees, fulfilling its accountability to its electorate. The implementation of federalism and the state structures also need to be structured according to federalism. This House is a permanent House. We are in the process where one-third of the honorable members are elected and one-third retire every two years. I congratulate the incoming new members and wish them success in their tenure. The National Assembly is one of the two Houses of the Federal Parliament, and even though the House of Representatives has been dissolved, we have been able to raise pressing issues of the public, discuss them, pass some bills in our regular activities, and discuss some reports. This is a matter of happiness. When the 18th session was suddenly adjourned, 7 bills originating in the National Assembly and even submitted as reports by the committee went into nullity. I feel that the state's investment and the efforts of all stakeholders have been wasted. Honorable Chairperson Sir, on Bhadra 23, 2082, the movement in the name of the new generation was against the closure of social media. The organizers also heard that the protest was infiltrated. On the same day, 19 young students lost their lives, which was a tragic aspect. On the 24th, the country's heritage sites were burned and vandalized. It seemed as if the entire country was burning. There was arson and vandalism of the executive, judiciary, legislature, business establishments, and even private homes. Participants were seen carrying away goods. I wonder how a Nepali heart could do this, destroying the country while wrapped in the country's flag. I also saw people proudly posting on social media. I believe that the individuals involved in such acts and crimes cannot be Nepali.

The environment has become insecure and it is felt that the Nepali heart is still afraid. Is burning down the country a means to resolve the shortcomings of the then government? Perhaps the change of power could have been achieved through other means. Those who made mistakes could have been punished. I feel irreparable damage has been done. I wonder how this will be compensated. Many mothers' laps have become empty. The country's invaluable heritage has been burnt. How will this irreparable damage be compensated? The injured and disabled are still in the hospital. It is true that the current civil government has formed a commission. It remains to be seen what kind of report the investigation commission under the chairmanship of Gauri Bahadur Karki will bring.

Honorable Chairperson, why and for whom was it done? The truth, the facts, and the reality must be revealed. Many suspicions have arisen. Shots were fired, human lives were lost. What did the Nepali people gain from this movement? What was achieved? The veil of mystery is yet to be lifted.

Good governance and corruption control remain as they are. Today, according to the report by Transparency International Nepal, corruption has increased in Nepal. This is a matter of concern. Honorable Chairperson, the new generation, the Gen Z, the ministers appointed in their name, was this how their work was? The Honorable Prime Minister is not at fault; he said he would go himself. It is not understood what the matter is. It is not as if a drama was staged with a trick. After taking responsibility to address the demands of the new generation to run the country, something must have been fulfilled. The regular election for the House of Representatives, scheduled for 2084, has been postponed to 2082. Was this movement held just to achieve this?

At this time, development works have stopped. Structures have been destroyed. There is an economic recession, and inflation is not visible. We are in such a situation, and I want to offer some suggestions to the National Assembly. I want to say that the National Assembly should always maintain its tradition, dignity, and identity. The name of the committee should not be changed repeatedly. The committee's budget should be allocated in a way that it can be spent regularly. The subject of public hearing kept in the rules could not be implemented. I want to draw the attention of the assembly to this as well. I urge all honorable members of the assembly to understand its importance and dignity equally and to be mindful of the time. Due to political ups and downs, the dissolution of the House of Representatives, and the ongoing legal proceedings, some bills that were discussed at various times and some that were even passed and awaiting authentication have gone to zero and are in a state of going to zero. Therefore, it is necessary and important, I think, to focus on how the obstacles seen in lawmaking can be overcome.

In the last session, the government introduced many bills, and we prioritized them. However, many bills are in a state of going to zero. We have brought the bills we have to a conclusion even in this adverse situation. We had three bills; there were four, but the government withdrew one, and we have brought three bills almost to a conclusion. Now we have to prioritize and work on laws to implement federalism. Federalism is constantly under attack. To counter this, these laws must be prioritized. The Legislation Management Committee has prepared a roster for the implementation of federalism, which we have submitted to the government. I urge the next session to monitor where it has reached and to monitor it. We have managed to make the constitution, which was left out in the Sudur Paschim region bordering Nepal, a part of our constitution during this period. I consider the moment of signing this decision as a historic opportunity. However, we have not been able to utilize that land yet. Due to continuous political instability, diplomatic work has not been managed properly. It is felt that there are problems in implementation due to this. Now, for political stability, it is necessary to amend the constitution if necessary for stability.

Honorable Chairperson, the National Assembly itself is an important assembly. Its importance is such that an attempt was made to tear up the constitution made by the people. The National Assembly succeeded in stopping that and sending a message that the constitution is active, I believe. If this assembly did not exist, there would have been a possibility of tampering with the constitution itself, I think. Many things cannot be said in these 12 minutes. Nevertheless, I got the opportunity to say a few things, even if symbolically. After coming to the National Assembly, I was very impressed by the implementation of the importance of the standard time set by the assembly as a form of discipline. The National Assembly has now established this as a recognized norm. During this period, this assembly has passed various proposals, including resolution proposals, and directed the government for their implementation. There is a need for pressure for their research, monitoring, and implementation. During this period, we have started interacting with our electoral constituency and voters at least once a year. We can do it many times, at least once. The National Assembly has made arrangements for this, and we have started it. I believe this will play a good role in the implementation of federalism, and we have interacted with provinces, local levels, etc., and understood their problems, listened to them, and made efforts for implementation. I want to say that the parliament should play a role in making this system even more effective. When we go to the provincial assemblies and local levels and discuss, their statement is that they have not been able to enact many laws due to the lack of federal laws. They also say that the federal government should quickly enact laws related to the implementation of federalism. The conclusions reached from this discussion have been kept by the assembly as its property, discussed, and now there is a need to pressure the state to do the work that needs to be done based on the issues raised, and to accelerate the work to be done by the state. We have already identified how many laws related to federalism are pending. The Legislation Committee has already submitted it to the government, and it has not started implementation. There is a need to put pressure on that as well. We have organized our zero hour, emergency hour, special hour, and provincial hour. Regarding zero hour, the honorable members have already spoken. Generally, we raise immediate problems and push the state. In emergency hour, if immediate issues need to be raised urgently, we request it from our seats. And all these works are progressing. In special hour, we have presented various political and ideological matters, and in provincial hour, we have kept it related to the programs we have advanced for interacting with the provinces. This provincial hour is said to be the last Friday of the month. This might need some adjustment. If it is not adjusted, sometimes there is a situation where it cannot be held. Therefore, I want to request the assembly to manage this to make it even more organized. We have managed the problems seen in delegated legislation by making legislation laws. Now, according to the legislation laws, laws will be made, and if the existing laws are not in accordance with the delegated legislation laws, they need to be organized, and arrangements have been made until Chaitra. The government needs to implement this.

Now, finally, during this period, the former Chairperson, the current Chairperson, the former and current Vice-Chairpersons, the members of the Assembly who will be coordinating, consulting, and cooperating during this period, the honorable members who will cooperate, the Secretary-General and all the staff, the security personnel, and all the staff present in the Parliament, everyone should cooperate with each other as we have been doing. I would like to request your cooperation for this and conclude my remarks by thanking you all. Thank you.

sections.name: Opening
sections.summary_en: The National Assembly meeting commenced at 13:18 hours under the chairpersonship of Narayan Prasad Dahal. The Zero Hour was scheduled, with each member allocated one minute to speak.

sections.summary_en: The Zero Hour concluded. The session announced that members retiring due to the completion of their six-year term would share their experiences. Honourable Devendra Dahal shared his reflections on his parliamentary and ministerial experiences, highlighting challenges and lessons learned.

speakers.topic: Parliamentary and ministerial experiences

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the consensus-based passing of bills in the National Assembly and the importance of inclusivity and the role of the assembly as an expert body. They highlight constitutional provisions that need correction to ensure fairness in bill processing between the House of Representatives and the National Assembly, citing an instance where a private bill was not discussed.

speakers.name: Honorable Chairperson
speakers.topic: Opening remarks and thanks

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker suggests focusing on state-essential issues, analytical presentations, and evidence-based discussions rather than solely political speeches. They propose discussions on Nepal's development, economic policies (agriculture, industry, trade), and the implementation of socialism as envisioned in the constitution.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker raises concerns about federalism, suggesting that public dissatisfaction is growing and questioning if the three-tiered government is a burden. They also discuss the role of remittances, the trade deficit, and the need for the assembly to provide direction for nation-building.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker reflects on their tenure, expresses gratitude, and emphasizes the need to maintain the assembly's dignity and establish it as an assembly of experts. They express confidence that the National Assembly will continue to provide valuable messages and guidance.

sections.name: Zero Hour
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Ganga Kumari Belbase praises the National Assembly for its punctuality and effective utilization of time, including Zero Hour and Special Time. She highlights the importance of Provincial Time in strengthening federalism and fostering cooperation among different levels of government.

sections.summary_en: The speaker emphasizes the National Assembly's role in cooperation and coordination, noting the collaborative work of its committees. They discuss the concept of unbroken succession in the assembly and the ongoing work of committees in monitoring, research, and evaluating government directives.

They highlight achievements in areas like federalism implementation, cancer prevention, and wildlife conservation, while also noting challenges and areas for improvement in law-making and implementation.

They reflect on their 6-year tenure, acknowledging both positive and negative experiences, and emphasize the importance of inclusivity and continuous improvement in parliamentary work.

sections.summary_en: The speaker reflects on the National Assembly's role, especially during the dissolution of the House of Representatives, and expresses regret over the loss of bills. They also condemn recent acts of vandalism and violence, questioning the perpetrators' nationality.

Suggestions are made for the National Assembly regarding committee budgets, public hearings, and expert rosters. The speaker also emphasizes the importance of ministries giving equal importance to both houses and following up on presented bills.
